vocabulary.definition: not shown or demonstrated to be true or valid
vocabulary.example: The scientist presented an unproven theory about the origins of the universe.

vocabulary.definition: using a figure of speech in which a term is used to describe something to which it is not literally applicable
vocabulary.example: When she said her heart was broken, she was speaking metaphorically about her emotional pain.

vocabulary.definition: to show that something is false or incorrect
vocabulary.example: The article debunked the popular myth that eating carrots improves eyesight.

vocabulary.definition: a questioning attitude or doubt towards something
vocabulary.example: She approached the new diet plan with scepticism, unsure if it would work for her.

vocabulary.definition: showing a lack of responsibility or consideration for the consequences of one's actions
vocabulary.example: It was irresponsible of the driver to text while driving, putting others at risk.

vocabulary.definition: able to be trusted to do or provide what is needed; dependable
vocabulary.example: The company has a reliable customer service team that always solves issues promptly.
